acme_integration: Hey @maria_support — we're seeing lots of 429s from the API today when we hit model rwd-3 with our batch jobs. It looks like they start after ~30s of steady traffic. No 401s, auth looks fine. Any hints?

maria_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a minimal repro (request pattern, rate, and context size)? Also which model spec (rwd-3-32k / rwd-3-64k) and token counts?

acme_integration: Repro below: we POST a set of parallel requests (10 parallel workers) every 1s, each request generates ~1200 tokens from a 6k context. Curl snippet:```bash
for i in {1..100}; do \n  seq 10 | xargs -P10 -I{} curl -s -X POST \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"rwd-3-64k","input":"<~6k context>","max_tokens":1200}' \n    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &\ndone
```
After ~30s we start to see 429s, ~40% of requests.

eli_engineer: Thanks — that pattern is a classic mixed fanout + long-context pressure. Two things to call out: per-model RPM/TPM and max concurrency interact with long context because tokens/session = higher resource footprint. On rwd-3-64k we have a lower concurrency cap per API key for large context sizes to protect multi-tenant latency.

maria_support: Can you confirm the exact HTTP response body for 429? Any retry-after header present?

acme_integration: Response: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"per-model capacity exceeded"}`. No Retry-After header.

sre_jordan: Quick note: when we throttle for per-model capacity we sometimes return 429 without Retry-After if it's a short burst window; reason is the backlog cleared by autoscaler in <60s. But we should surface X-RateLimit-* headers. I'll check logs for your API key.

support-bot: Deploy notice: scaled dedicated pool for rwd-3-64k at 2765432119 by autoscaler (reason: sustained enqueue).

eli_engineer: From our side, likely root causes: 1) your parallel worker count + 1s cadence creates sustained concurrent in-flight requests > model concurrency quota for large contexts, 2) TPM window exhaustion due to token-heavy responses, 3) ephemeral queueing causes the runtime to drop new inflight requests.

eli_engineer: Quick repro we ran (simulated): 10 workers * avg 1300 tokens/output -> ~13k tokens/sec aggregate => hits TPM ceilings for the tier and triggers short-term drops. Also concurrency cap is per-connection/stream; with large KV caches each slot uses more GPU memory so concurrency cap effectively lower.

maria_support: Recommended mitigations:
- Reduce parallelism or add jitter/stagger (e.g., randomized start delay 0-500ms).
- Add exponential backoff on 429s (start 200ms -> 2s max) and retry limited times.
- Trim context where possible (move historical context to embeddings + retrieval or summarize).
- Use streaming where possible to reduce peak token allocation per request.
- Consider pinning to a smaller-context variant for high-concurrency paths.

acme_integration: Is there a way to pre-check capacity before sending big batches? We want to avoid hitting 429s which break our job orchestration.

eli_engineer: Two approaches:
1) Implement a local token budget: estimate tokens per response and cap concurrent requests accordingly.
2) Use our /v1/health or token-estimate endpoint (preflight) to batch-check capacity — we can also surface per-model remaining-rpm/rpm-burst in upcoming console flags. For now, do a light head request (small payload) to detect if the model is currently queued.

maria_support: Also, if you need sustained high throughput with large contexts we can discuss Dedicated capacity or Reserved slots — that removes multi-tenant throttles and gives stable concurrency. I'll open a ticket for a Dedicated eval if you want.

acme_integration: OK thanks. One more: we sometimes see 401 + 429 overlap when tokens are rotated in our pipeline. Could auth flaps cause rate-limiting?

eli_engineer: If your API key is invalid briefly you might see 401s which are not counted toward rate limits. However, if you retry immediately with a fresh key and flood the server you can trigger rate limits. Best practice: detect 401s and pause retries until key rotation completes.

sre_jordan: Follow-up: I pulled your API key trace — we saw a spike of enqueues at 2765432118 that matched your pattern. We also emitted internal metric per_model.concurrent_slots = 32 (limit for large context). Your pattern tried to open ~44 concurrent slots. That explains the 429 drop rate.

maria_support: Action items:
- acme_integration: add jitter and reduce parallel workers from 10 -> 6 and enable exponential backoff for 429s. Try trimming context by 20% where possible.
- eli_engineer / sre_jordan: follow up about exposing a clearer Retry-After/X-RateLimit header for short burst throttles.

acme_integration: Will implement changes and report back within the day. Thanks for the clear explanation and mitigation steps :thumbsup:

maria_support: Happy to help — we'll keep monitoring and I put a watch on your key for the rest of the day.
